title: RBAC & Audit -> SIEM Fallback Procedures and Evidence Automation SOP
content:
Purpose:
This runbook documents a concise, actionable SOP for on-call engineers and security responders when RBAC v2 events, audit logging, or SIEM exports fail or produce incomplete evidence. It combines human triage steps, automated evidence-capture fallbacks, and post-incident tagging guidance so incidents impacting access control or log fidelity can be investigated within SLAs.

Scope and when to use:
- Applies to incidents where: RBAC enforcement anomalies are observed (permission denials that look incorrect, privilege escalation alerts), audit logs are missing or malformed for relevant time windows, or SIEM exporters (ELK / Splunk / Chronicle connectors) fail to deliver expected events.
- Not for: pure application bugs unrelated to auth/audit, or routine SIEM alert noise that has been triaged to known false positives.

Quick decision flow (two-minute checklist):
1) Confirm whether the issue is enforcement (access rejected/allowed incorrectly) or observability (logs missing/incorrect).
2) If enforcement: disable broad remediation (do not change RBAC rules globally). Escalate to eng-platform if customers are impacted.
3) If observability: immediately capture live evidence (see Capture Evidence section) and check exporter health.
4) If SIEM exporter failing: trigger automated fallback collector and route raw files to the secure evidence bucket.

Roles & responsibilities:
- On-call SRE / Security On-call: initial triage, evidence capture, containment decisions, create incident ticket.
- Platform Engineering (RBAC owner): diagnose policy engine, evaluate policy diffs, rollback if a bad policy push is the cause.
- Observability / Logging: investigate exporter connectivity, re-ingest backlog, validate schema mapping.
- Incident Lead: coordinate stakeholders, author initial incident summary, set P0/P1 as needed.

Key SLAs:
- 15 minutes: initial triage and incident ticket creation with evidence location.
- 60 minutes: automated fallback collector deployed (if exporter still failing) and raw evidence archived.
- 8 hours: high-level incident brief to stakeholders with mitigation steps.

Initial triage steps (detailed):
1) Confirm symptoms: reproduce a sample event where possible (e.g., have a test user attempt the same action). Note timestamps in UTC.
2) Check RBAC policy change log: git history and deployment pipeline (owner: eng-platform). Command: git log --pretty=oneline --since=24h configs/rbac/*.yaml
3) Inspect runtime enforcement logs (authz service): curl https://internal-authz/redwood/v1/logs?user=TEST_USER&since=2025-02-14T00:00:00Z (internal only). Look for decision outcomes: allow/deny, matched_rules.
4) Verify audit log presence: query the primary audit store for the same time window. Example Elasticsearch query (pseudo):
   POST /_search
   {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"match": {"request.user.id": "test-user-id"}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "2025-02-14T09:30:00Z","lte": "2025-02-14T09:45:00Z"}}}]}}}
5) If logs missing, check ingestion pipeline: exporter pods, connector metrics, and retention tier. kubectl -n logging get pods -l app=audit-exporter

Capture Evidence - prioritized actions (immutable-first):
- Goal: collect raw inputs that prove what happened (requests, policy decisions, system-level network flows) before any state drift.

1) Live API audit pull (preferred):
- Use internal audit API which returns canonical audit entries for timeframe. Example: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${AUDIT_API_TOKEN}" "https://audit-api.internal.redwood/v1/entries?start=2025-02-14T09:30:00Z&end=2025-02-14T09:45:00Z&filter=user:test-user-id" > /tmp/evidence/audit_entries.json
- Save file to secure evidence bucket: gsutil cp /tmp/evidence/audit_entries.json gs://redwood-evidence/INC-<id>/raw/

2) Policy engine trace capture (if enforcement suspected):
- Enable short-lived debug trace for policy engine for the user and action (this can be noisy; limit to 10 minutes). Endpoint: POST https://authz.internal/trace {"user":"test-user-id","action":"read:model"}
- Save trace output as trace_<ts>.json and upload.

3) Network-level evidence:
- Capture tcpdump or flow logs on relevant nodes briefly: sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/evidence/tcpdump.pcap host <model-server-ip> and rotate after capture. Upload.

4) Service-level logs:
- Collect container logs (kubectl logs) for all implicated pods with --since flag. 
- Example: kubectl -n inference logs deployment/model-gateway --since=30m > /tmp/evidence/model-gateway.log

Automated fallback collector (when SIEM exports are down):
- Trigger the lightweight fallback collector (run by on-call):
  /opt/tools/fallback-collector --start --window 00:60 --filter 'resource:authz OR resource:audit' --out /tmp/evidence/fallback-raw-<ts>.tar.gz
- Fallback collector will hit the internal audit API and pull raw entries, package them with minimal metadata, sign the archive, and attempt upload. If upload fails, collectors keep local copies on encrypted volume and report via pager duty.

SIEM Exporter troubleshooting checklist:
1) Health: kubectl -n logging get pods -l app=audit-exporter => check restarts and ready status.
2) Connectivity: curl -v http(s) to SIEM endpoint (use integration test key) and confirm 200.
3) Backlog: check exporter queue length and last-seen timestamp. Metric: audit_exporter_queue_size.
4) Schema errors: exporter logs often show mapping failures. Grep for "mapping" or "schema mismatch".
5) Re-ingest: once fixed, trigger incremental reingest job: POST /internal/reingest/audit?start=2025-02-14T09:00:00Z&end=2025-02-14T11:00:00Z

Audit log schema reference (canonical fields) - validate these are present in raw evidence and SIEM index mapping:
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC string
- request_id: unique request UUID (correlate across services)
- actor_id: user or service principal id
- actor_type: user | service | system
- resource: resource identifier (model:<id> | route:<id> | project:<id>)
- action: verb string (authorize, create, delete, exec, token_issue)
- outcome: success | failure | denied
- matched_policy: policy id or null
- raw_payload: truncated/hashed request body for sensitive ops
- ip_address: client IP if available
- session_id: session correlation id
- svc_version: service git SHA or build id

Common schema mismatch symptoms and fixes:
- Missing request_id or actor_id: likely older SDKs or misconfigured sidecars. Fix: bump SDK, add GUID generator, and reingest if raw payload contains correlating fields.
- action is free-text causing high-cardinality: normalize at exporter using a mapping table.
- timestamps off by hours: check clock drift on nodes (chrony/ntpd).

Forensic preservation and chain-of-evidence notes:
- All evidence uploaded to gs://redwood-evidence/INC-<id>/ must be write-once (use object versioning and retention policy).
- Name files with ISO timestamps and include SHA256 metadata. Example: audit_entries_2025-02-14T09:30:00Z.json sha256:abcd...
- Document all manual actions in the incident ticket with timestamps and actor names.

Ticketing & incident metadata template (copy into ticket description):
- Short summary: 1-line description
- Impact: customer-visible? yes/no; affected clusters/regions
- Timeline: bullet list with UTC timestamps
- Evidence location: gs://redwood-evidence/INC-<id>/raw/
- Initial mitigation steps taken
- Suggested owner for next steps

Post-incident review checklist (to be completed within 72 hours):
- Verify reingest completed and SIEM indices reflect missing events.
- Confirm RBAC policy changes (if any) are reverted or documented and attached to the ticket.
- Root cause (one-paragraph) and action items with owners and due dates.
- Add regression test(s) to CI: e.g., synthetic audit event generation and exporter smoke test.
- Update this runbook with any new commands, URLs, or automation IDs used during the incident.

Helpful queries & snippets (examples for common SIEMs) - adapt to your SIEM flavor:
- Elastic / ES DSL (pseudo):
  {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"match": {"request_id": "<uuid>"}}]}}}
- Splunk: index=audit source="authz" request_id="<uuid>" | table _time actor_id action outcome resource
- Kibana KQL: request_id : "<uuid>" OR actor_id : "test-user-id"

Housekeeping & runbook hygiene:
- Owner for this doc: security-oncall rotation (see team rota) - currently Aisha Patel.
- Quarterly review required: validate exporter integration tests, update any changed endpoints or bucket names.
- If you add new automation scripts, include unit tests and place them under github.com/redwood-inference/automation/collectors with a README and review by Observability team.

Open questions / TODOs (working items):
- [ ] Add a signed attest file from fallback collector recording the collector version and checksum (vendor request from legal).
- [ ] Add end-to-end synthetic test for exporter reingest (JIRA: JIRA-OBS-223).
- [ ] Decide retention policy for fallback-local copies (currently 30 days; legal to confirm).

Appendix A - Example fallback-collector command and minimal output:
- Command: /opt/tools/fallback-collector --start --window 60 --out /tmp/fallback-2025-02-14.tar.gz --filter "resource:authz"
- Minimal output snippet: {"collected": 182, "earliest": "2025-02-14T09:01:00Z", "latest": "2025-02-14T10:01:00Z", "archive_sha256": "e3b0c44298fc1c..."}

Appendix B - Minimal incident summary template (for external stakeholders)
- What happened (one line)
- When (UTC)
- Who was impacted (services/regions)
- What we did (mitigation)
- Next steps (what we will prevent in future)
- Contact for follow-up: security-oncall@redwood.ai

If you follow this SOP and there are gaps, capture them immediately as a TODO in the incident ticket and file a small postmortem action item titled "Runbook gap: <short description>".

Notes to on-call: this doc is intentionally prescriptive but conservative — do not perform wide RBAC rollbacks without platform approval. If customers are impacted, prefer scope-limited fixes and quick mitigations while we debug root cause.

Last updated by Aisha Patel on 2025-03-01 (minor clarifications to fallback-collector invocation).
